title: Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE — Premium Revision Paper #12

pages.quiz:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #12
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which sentence uses 'the' correctly for a best one? (1 mark)
   A. She is a the tallest girl.
   B. She is tall the girl.
   C. She is tallest a girl.
   D. She is the tallest girl.

2. Choose the correct pair: '___ tall boy and ___ old woman.' (1 mark)
   A. A, an
   B. An, an
   C. An, a
   D. The, an

3. What does 'DOB' mean on a form? (1 mark)
   A. Day of business
   B. Date of book
   C. Duty of boy
   D. Date of birth

4. A simile compares two things using (1 mark)
   A. like or as
   B. if or then
   C. but or and
   D. who or which

5. Which word stays the same in the plural? (1 mark)
   A. sheep
   B. goat
   C. hen
   D. cow

6. What is the plural of 'baby'? (1 mark)
   A. babys
   B. babies
   C. baby
   D. babyes

7. Which is the more polite request? (1 mark)
   A. I want the pen.
   B. Pen now.
   C. May I borrow your pen, please?
   D. Give me your pen.

8. Why did the woman say Neema's mother had taught her good manners? (1 mark)
   A. Because Neema spoke and acted politely
   B. Because Neema was tall
   C. Because Neema was late
   D. Because Neema was rich

9. We answer comprehension questions best in (1 mark)
   A. full sentences
   B. drawings only
   C. numbers only
   D. one letter

10. What should you use first when learning neat print script? (1 mark)
   A. A brush
   B. A pencil
   C. A felt pen
   D. A marker

11. What does a foot bridge help people to do? (1 mark)
   A. Park cars
   B. Cross a road safely by walking over it
   C. Drive fast
   D. Carry luggage

12. Which pronoun replaces 'Ali and I'? (1 mark)
   A. you
   B. they
   C. we
   D. he

13. Which is a sentence starter for sharing a story? (1 mark)
   A. To whom it may concern...
   B. Yours faithfully...
   C. My favourite part was...
   D. Dear Sir...

14. Why should you return borrowed books on time? (1 mark)
   A. To forget the title
   B. To make the book dirty
   C. So others can read them too
   D. Because books are heavy

15. About how long is a Grade 4 narrative composition? (1 mark)
   A. 10 words
   B. 60 to 80 words
   C. 5 words
   D. 1000 words

16. In the story shape, the highest point is (1 mark)
   A. the title
   B. the exciting part
   C. the last full stop
   D. the date

17. At the end of a yes or no question, the voice usually (1 mark)
   A. stays low always
   B. rises
   C. stops
   D. falls

18. Which noun is countable? (1 mark)
   A. mango
   B. money
   C. time
   D. rice

19. Why do two learners write different stories from the same pictures? (1 mark)
   A. They copy each other
   B. Each writer uses different words and ideas
   C. One is always wrong
   D. The pictures are blank

20. Which word has the soft buzzing sound /ʒ/ in the middle? (1 mark)
   A. yam
   B. bridge
   C. television
   D. jug

21. To retell a story, which things should you say? (1 mark)
   A. Who, where, what happened and how it ended
   B. Only the last word
   C. The page numbers
   D. Only the title

22. Which is written correctly? (1 mark)
   A. we climbed mount elgon!
   B. we climbed mount elgon
   C. We climbed mount elgon,
   D. We climbed Mount Elgon.

23. Which of these is a proper noun? (1 mark)
   A. hill
   B. town
   C. river
   D. Mombasa

24. What is a plough? (1 mark)
   A. A place for storing tools
   B. A small insect that damages crops
   C. A tool or machine used to turn over soil before planting
   D. A kind of fertilizer

25. Which is a positive statement? (1 mark)
   A. The shed is locked.
   B. The shed isn't locked.
   C. The shed was never locked.
   D. The shed is not locked.

26. Which is the correct negative of 'We planted beans'? (1 mark)
   A. We didn't planted beans.
   B. We not planted beans.
   C. We don't planted beans.
   D. We didn't plant beans.

27. Which sentence has a comma before the spoken words? (1 mark)
   A. Mother said. "Please close the door"
   B. Mother, said "Please close the door."
   C. Mother said "Please close the door"
   D. Mother said, "Please close the door."

28. Which is a nonverbal cue that shows you are listening? (1 mark)
   A. Looking out of the window
   B. Looking at the speaker and nodding
   C. Turning your back
   D. Talking to a friend

29. Which pair differs in the sounds /s/ and /ʃ/? (1 mark)
   A. live and leave
   B. sea and she
   C. sit and seat
   D. go and no

30. Which word has the sound /aʊ/? (1 mark)
   A. cat
   B. hot
   C. crowd
   D. bell

31. Which is a safe habit when searching online? (1 mark)
   A. Clicking every pop-up
   B. Using sites your teacher approves
   C. Telling strangers your password
   D. Sharing your address

32. Which key words would help you find out how netball is played? (1 mark)
   A. my address
   B. netball rules for children
   C. password
   D. free prizes

33. Which question is correct for asking about the owner of some boots? (1 mark)
   A. Who boots are these?
   B. Whose are boot these?
   C. Whose is these boots?
   D. Whose boots are these?

34. Which is a good way to learn a hard spelling? (1 mark)
   A. Copy it wrongly
   B. Guess it every time
   C. Look, cover, write and check
   D. Never write it

35. What is hesitation in speaking? (1 mark)
   A. Using gestures
   B. Speaking clearly
   C. Stopping or saying 'um' and 'er'
   D. Speaking loudly

36. Which word has the short vowel /ʌ/? (1 mark)
   A. floor
   B. sport
   C. mother
   D. door

37. Which situation fits 'Little by little fills the measure'? (1 mark)
   A. Losing a shoe
   B. Picking up a little rubbish every day until the compound is clean
   C. Sleeping late
   D. Getting a big prize at once

38. Which time word often goes with the present perfect? (1 mark)
   A. yesterday
   B. already
   C. last week
   D. in 2010

39. Which sentence uses the right tense with the time word 'yesterday'? (1 mark)
   A. I have saw him yesterday.
   B. I have seen him yesterday.
   C. I saw him yesterday.
   D. I had seen him yesterday now.

40. What sounds does the letter x usually make in 'box'? (1 mark)
   A. /z/
   B. /ks/
   C. /f/
   D. /gz/

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Write directions to walk from the school to the market on the map in the lesson. (3 marks)

42. Complete the sentences: (a) We have enough plates ___ (eat) the meal. (b) There is enough rice ___ (feed) the guests. (2 marks)

43. Give three strategies that help you read more fluently. (3 marks)

44. Write four words with double consonants and four words with blends. (4 marks)

45. Explain what the saying 'A stitch in time saves nine' teaches. (2 marks)

46. Write two minimal pairs for /t/ and /d/. (2 marks)

47. Replace the second mention with a pronoun: 'Neema saw the bridge. Neema liked the bridge.' (2 marks)

48. Name two visuals you can find in a newspaper. (2 marks)

49. Why is it important to interpret road signs correctly? (2 marks)

50. Explain what Baraka learnt from his grandmother. (4 marks)

51. Write two sentences using a simile of your own about a celebration. (4 marks)

52. Name two things that a good listener does when a story is read aloud. (2 marks)

53. Draw a mind map in words: put 'Keeping Fit' in the centre and give four branches. (4 marks)

54. Rewrite in the past tense: 'Baraka types a message and clicks Send.' (2 marks)

55. Write two sentences beginning 'I would like to be' and give a reason in each. (3 marks)

56. Explain what we learn from the story about honesty. (3 marks)

57. Describe how to skim and how to scan a passage. (4 marks)

58. Write three sentences about your family or school: one comparative, one superlative and one with two adjectives in the right order. (3 marks)

59. Write three sentences about a car near a bridge using one subject pronoun, one object pronoun and one possessive pronoun. (3 marks)

60. Sort into countable and uncountable: rice, mango, time, book. (2 marks)

61. In the passage 'The Purse in the Market', what did the purse contain? (2 marks)

62. Explain why it is important to put the stress on the right syllable. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #12 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — She is the tallest girl.
   We use the before superlative words such as tallest.

2. A — A, an
   Tall starts with a consonant sound, old starts with a vowel sound.

3. D — Date of birth
   DOB is short for date of birth.

4. A — like or as
   A simile uses like or as, for example as brave as a lion.

5. A — sheep
   Sheep is both singular and plural.

6. B — babies
   A consonant comes before y, so change y to i and add es.

7. C — May I borrow your pen, please?
   It uses may I and please.

8. A — Because Neema spoke and acted politely
   Her actions showed good manners.

9. A — full sentences
   Full sentences show that we understand.

10. B — A pencil
   A pencil allows you to rub out mistakes.

11. B — Cross a road safely by walking over it
   It goes over the road.

12. C — we
   We includes the speaker and another person.

13. C — My favourite part was...
   It helps you tell what you liked.

14. C — So others can read them too
   It shows responsibility and fairness.

15. B — 60 to 80 words
   The design asks for about 60 to 80 words.

16. B — the exciting part
   Events rise to an exciting part.

17. B — rises
   Yes or no questions usually end with a rise.

18. A — mango
   We can count mangoes.

19. B — Each writer uses different words and ideas
   Each writer has a different voice.

20. C — television
   'Television' has /ʒ/. 'Jug' and 'bridge' have /ʤ/.

21. A — Who, where, what happened and how it ended
   A retelling covers characters, place, events and ending.

22. D — We climbed Mount Elgon.
   The first word and the mountain name need capitals, and a statement ends with a full stop.

23. D — Mombasa
   Mombasa is the name of a particular town.

24. C — A tool or machine used to turn over soil before planting
   The plough breaks up soil ready for planting.

25. A — The shed is locked.
   It has no negative word.

26. D — We didn't plant beans.
   After didn't, use the base form plant.

27. D — Mother said, "Please close the door."
   A comma comes after 'said' before the spoken words.

28. B — Looking at the speaker and nodding
   Eye contact and nods show attention.

29. B — sea and she
   'Sea' has /s/ and 'she' has /ʃ/.

30. C — crowd
   'Crowd' has the diphthong /aʊ/, as in 'cow'.

31. B — Using sites your teacher approves
   Approved sites and private details keep you safe.

32. B — netball rules for children
   Good key words describe the topic you want.

33. D — Whose boots are these?
   'Whose' is followed by a noun.

34. C — Look, cover, write and check
   Cover-write-check builds memory.

35. C — Stopping or saying 'um' and 'er'
   Practise to hesitate less.

36. C — mother
   'Mother' has the short /ʌ/.

37. B — Picking up a little rubbish every day until the compound is clean
   Small efforts add up.

38. B — already
   'Already' fits the present perfect; finished-time words do not.

39. C — I saw him yesterday.
   Use the simple past with a finished time such as yesterday.

40. B — /ks/
   In 'box', x says k and s together.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Walk east to the roundabout, go straight east across the foot bridge and you will reach the market.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for east, 1 mark for the roundabout and 1 mark for the foot bridge and market.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) to eat (b) to feed
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Preview the text; read in phrases; follow the punctuation; re-read; read along with a model.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Double: letter, dinner, apple, bottle. Blends: train, snake, clap, flag.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct group of two words, up to 4.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: It teaches us to fix a small problem early, before it becomes a big problem.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fixing early and 1 mark for avoiding a bigger problem.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: ten, den and tin, din.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Neema saw the bridge. She liked it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for she and 1 mark for it.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any two: photographs, cartoons, maps, charts, advertisements.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: Signs warn us of danger and tell us what to do, so misunderstanding one could cause an accident.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for what signs do and 1 mark for the danger of misunderstanding.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: He learnt that ugali and tea are not enough. A balanced diet with energy foods, body-building foods, fruit and vegetables and clean water keeps a person strong and healthy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct points.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: The cake was as sweet as honey. The children danced like leaves in the wind.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each sentence with a correct simile.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: Look at the speaker; do not interrupt; think about what you hear; ask a question when the speaker finishes (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Centre: Keeping Fit. Branches: exercise, healthy food, sleep, clean water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the centre and 1 for each branch.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: Baraka typed a message and clicked Send.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each verb.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: I would like to be a doctor because I want to help sick people. I would like to be a runner because I love sport.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence with reason, and 1 for accuracy.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Honesty means returning what belongs to others. Neema returned the purse and refused a reward, and her mother said honesty is a great treasure.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for the example, 1 mark for the message.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: To skim, look at the title, pictures and the first sentence of each paragraph to get the main idea. To scan, look quickly for key words to find a particular fact.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for skimming and 2 marks for scanning.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: My brother is taller than I am. He is the tallest boy in his class. He has a big round bag.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: It has bright head lights. The bridge protects us. The car is theirs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: Countable: mango, book. Uncountable: rice, time.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each group.

61. (2 marks)
   Answer: It had some coins and a card with the name Mrs Achieng Odhiambo.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the coins and 1 mark for the card.

62. (2 marks)
   Answer: Wrong stress can make a word hard to understand, and it can change the word from a noun to a verb.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.
